1.?

Find f′(x) if f(x)=excsc⁡x.

M
Wed, Aug 5th @ 2:14 PM|Elapsed: 2:49Correct

We calculate the derivative using the product rule, as follows:

f′(x)=ddx(excsc⁡x)=ex(csc⁡x)+ex(−csc⁡xcot⁡x)=excsc⁡x(1−cot⁡x)

2.?
Find h′(x) if h(x)=4xcsc⁡(x).
h′(x)=
4csc⁡(x)−4xcsc⁡(x)cot⁡(x)
M
Wed, Aug 5th @ 2:16 PM|Elapsed: 1:27Correct

We calculate the derivative using the product rule, as follows:

h′(x)=ddx(4xcsc⁡(x))=4(csc⁡(x))+(4x)(−csc⁡(x)cot⁡(x))=4csc⁡(x)−4xcsc⁡(x)cot⁡(x)

3.?

Find f′(x) if f(x)=cot⁡xx2.

M
Wed, Aug 5th @ 2:20 PM|Elapsed: 3:25Correct

We calculate the derivative using the quotient rule, as follows:

f′(x)=ddx(cot⁡xx2)=(−csc2⁡x)⋅x2−cot⁡x⋅(2x)x4=−xcsc2⁡x−2cot⁡xx3

4.?

Find f′(π6) if f(x)=−6cot⁡x.

H
Wed, Aug 5th @ 2:24 PM|Elapsed: 4:04Correct

First, we just take the constant out of the derivative and use the result for the derivative of cot⁡x, as follows: f′(x)=ddx(−6cot⁡x)=−6(−csc2⁡x)=6csc2⁡x

Then, we substitute x=π6 in the derivative and get f′(π6)=6csc2⁡(π6)=6(2)2=24.

6.?

Calculate dydx if y=3x2+cos⁡x−3sec⁡x.

E
Wed, Aug 5th @ 2:30 PM|Elapsed: 1:47Correct

We take the derivative of each term and then add them, as follows:

dydx=ddx(3x−2+cos⁡x−3sec⁡x)=−2⋅3x−3+(−sin⁡x)−3sec⁡xtan⁡x=−6x−3−sin⁡x−3sec⁡xtan⁡x=−6x3−sin⁡x−3sec⁡xtan⁡x

7.?

Calculate dydx if y=sec⁡x4x.

M
Wed, Aug 5th @ 2:33 PM|Elapsed: 2:57Correct

We calculate the derivative using the quotient rule, as follows:

dydx=ddx(sec⁡x4x)=(sec⁡xtan⁡x)(4x)−(sec⁡x)(4)(4x)2=4xsec⁡xtan⁡x−4sec⁡x16x2=4(xsec⁡xtan⁡x−sec⁡x)16x2=xsec⁡xtan⁡x−sec⁡x4x2

KP 4. Finding the Slope of the Tangent at a Point of a Function Involving Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions
8.?

Find the slope of y=f(x) at x=π4 if f(x)=xcot⁡x.

M
Wed, Aug 5th @ 2:35 PM|Elapsed: 1:57Correct

First, we take the derivative using the product rule:

dydx=ddx(xcot⁡x)=cot⁡x+x(−csc2⁡x)=cot⁡x−xcsc2⁡x

Then, we substitute x=π4 in the derivative and get

dydx|π/4=cot⁡(π4)−π4csc2⁡(π4)=1−π4⋅(2)2=1−π2.

9.?
Find the slope m of y=g(x) at x=π2 if g(x)=csc⁡xcot⁡x.
m=
−1
M
Wed, Aug 5th @ 2:41 PM|Elapsed: 5:17Correct

First, we calculate the derivative using the product rule and sum rule:

g′(x)=ddx(csc⁡xcot⁡x)=(−csc⁡xcot⁡x)(cot⁡x)+(csc⁡x)(−csc2⁡x)=−csc⁡x(cot2⁡x+csc2⁡x)

Now, we substitute x=π2 and evaluate the slope m:

m=g′(π2)=−csc⁡(π2)[cot2⁡(π2)+csc2⁡(π2)]=−1⋅(02+12)=−1
